text:
Here are the best open-ear earbuds for running, based on Runner's World, WIRED, and SoundGuys. Prices are what those sites listed, so check them at checkout.

## Top picks

**Best overall clip-on: [Shokz OpenDots 2](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0GQ3H9YLF), about $200**
- WIRED named it best overall. Runner's World picked it as best for long runs.
- Battery is 10 hours per earbud, or 40 hours with the case. It is rated IP57.
- The earbuds sense which ear they're in, so either one goes in either ear.
- One Runner's World tester got a small zap while running in heavy rain, despite the rating.
- Sources: [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/), [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)

**Best sound: [Bose Ultra Open Earbuds](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0CPFVB5VN), about $199 on sale (list price $299)**
- Runner's World ranked it best overall. WIRED says it has clearer, more defined sound than most competitors.
- It has physical buttons, which are easier to use mid-run than touch controls.
- Battery is about 7 hours, and it is only IPX4, so it's a weaker choice for heavy rain.
- Runner's World says Bose plans to release a new open-ear model soon. If you're not in a hurry, it may be worth waiting.

**Best bone conduction: [Shokz OpenRun Pro 2](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0D2HKCMBP), about $180 list, with sales near $125**
- It sits on your cheekbones, so your ears stay fully open, which is the most awareness of any style.
- Battery is 12 hours and it is rated IP55. WIRED says its sound is clearer than most small open earbuds, especially in noisy places.
- The band can get in the way of hats, hoods, or low ponytails. Bass is lighter than on the speaker-style earbuds.

**Best value for runners: [Soundcore AeroClip](https://www.amazon.com/Soundcore-AeroClip-Open-Ear-Earbuds-Crystal-Clear/dp/B0HFJ7NVPB) / AeroClip 2, about $130–$170**
- WIRED's runner-up is the original AeroClip. It is light, stable on the ear, and rated IP55.
- Runner's World liked the newer AeroClip 2 for battery life (10–11 hours) and call quality. Its bass is on the light side.

## Budget picks
- **[JLab Flex Open](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0D8K3WN1S), about $40:** Runner's World's best budget pick. It's comfortable and fits well, but has less bass and detail than the pricier pairs.
- **[Soundpeats PearlClip Pro](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Soundpeats+PearlClip+Pro), about $50:** WIRED's cheap pick. The app and touch controls are a bit finicky. I didn't find a direct product page, so that link is an Amazon search.
- **[Soundcore AeroFit 2](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Soundcore+AeroFit+2), about $80–$100:** SoundGuys' budget pick. It has adjustable ear hooks, IP55, and wireless charging. I didn't find a direct product page, so that link is an Amazon search.
- **[Nothing Ear (Open)](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0DGLL5CWK), about $99:** SoundGuys' best overall, with strong bass for the category. It's slim and rated IP54.

## How to choose
- **Maximum awareness, ponytail and hat flexibility not a priority:** Shokz OpenRun Pro 2.
- **Marathon training or rainy runs:** Shokz OpenDots 2.
- **Music-first:** Bose Ultra Open.
- **Unsure about open-ear:** JLab Flex Open. Fit varies by ear shape, so check the return policy.

Open-ear designs don't guarantee safety. Loud music can still mask cars or cyclists, so keep the volume moderate.

I also saw a Soundcore AeroFit 2 promo-code page in the search results. I couldn't verify it, so I left it out. Check Soundcore's own store for current deals.

 Open earbuds are the big new thing in headphone land. Unlike in-ear variants, open earbuds are like tiny speakers that rest on the ear and let outside sound in naturally, so you can fully hear the world around you. Some use a hook style that wraps around the back of your ear, while others are clip-ons that look more like statement-piece earrings. Style aside, they are excellent for anyone who finds traditional earbuds uncomfortable or wants full environmental awareness for activities like running, biking, or even just doing chores around the house.
 I've tested dozens of models since 2022, and while I still recommend having a pair of [noise-canceling earbuds](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-noise-canceling-earbuds/), I also love open earbuds for specific use cases.
